ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZSowbA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC5zbE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 15, "title": "Implement shared S-DSP noise generation and per-voice NON routing", "body": "## Problem

The DSP cannot produce hardware noise. `Dsp` has no noise-generator state, and every active voice uses Gaussian-interpolated BRR output regardless of NON (`$3D`). Software selecting noise therefore receives the wrong waveform.

At baseline `63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3`, see [DSP state and initialization](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L17-L40) and [unconditional BRR interpolation and mixing](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L208-L225).

Issue #13 supplied the shared rate scheduler needed by noise but explicitly left noise unimplemented. Implementing its consumer is a bounded next step; it does not duplicate the completed envelope scheduler or direct-color improvements. The supplied context lists no open Issues.

## Expected outcome

Implement one shared S-DSP noise generator and route its output to voices selected by NON, within the existing sample-level DSP architecture.

Specification references already identified by the repository are [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), specifically the DSP NON/FLG, noise-generator and ADSR/Gain-and-Noise rate descriptions, and [Anomie's S-DSP Doc, updated by jwdonal, revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0), particularly COUNTERS and SOUND GENERATION. Record section-specific attribution and independent vector derivations in the implementation's validation evidence; use specification facts rather than importing emulator implementation code.

Required semantics:

- Maintain one 15-bit noise shift register, initialized to `$4000` when constructing/resetting the emulator's DSP state. On an eligible noise event, compute `feedback = (old_bit0 XOR old_bit1)` and `next = (old >> 1) | (feedback << 14)`. Convert the held state to the voice input as signed 16-bit `state << 1`.
- Select the noise rate with FLG (`$6C`) bits 0–4. Reuse the existing shared counter and its rate offsets. Rate 0 holds the current noise value; rate 31 advances every sample. Rate changes use the existing counter phase without restarting it.
- Preserve the [Issue #13 sample convention](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/docs/issue-13-validation.md#specification-and-counter-convention): decrement the shared counter before polling. Advance noise once per stereo sample, before voice source selection, so all selected voices use the same held value.
- NON bit `n` selects noise for voice `n`, replacing interpolation before envelope multiplication. Apply the existing envelope scaling, signed sample rounding, OUTX publication, signed stereo volumes and EON routing to that selected source. Unselected voices retain BRR output.
- Noise frequency is independent of voice pitch. Continue the existing pitch/BRR progression and ENDX handling while noise is selected; NON must not suspend decoding or bypass BRR end behavior.
- Noise processing continues without selected/active voices and while muted. KON, KOFF, NON writes and FLG voice reset do not reseed the generator or restart its shared clock. Preserve voice silence during key-on delay, voice reset and completed release. Distinguish FLG voice reset from reconstructing the emulator's DSP state.

Scope is functional noise generation at sample boundaries. DSP subcycle register sampling, SPC bus timing, PMON implementation, hidden-envelope corrections and reference echo saturation are non-goals.

## Context and reproduction

The [existing rate tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L323-L391) verify scheduler events, but no test verifies noise-state advancement or NON routing. The [APU](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L152-L155) produces one DSP sample every 32 SPC clocks. The [original uploaded SPC700 envelope guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_envelope.rs) provides an established firmware-free integration-test pattern.

A focused reproduction is an active direct-GAIN voice with zero-valued looping BRR data, audible volumes, echo disabled and its NON bit set. The baseline remains silent because it interpolates zeros. Expected noise-derived OUTX/PCM must instead match independent numerical vectors.

This evaluation used repository inspection and supplied context only; no tests were executed or external specifications fetched. Historical passes in the Issue #13 validation record are preservation evidence, not noise verification.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the required generator, rate selection and NON routing without a separate rate clock or unrelated architectural changes.
- [ ] Add original numerical tests that fail on the baseline and pass with the implementation. Include literal initial sequence vectors through feedback and sign changes, the nonzero 32,767-update cycle, and signed source/envelope/OUTX/PCM expectations. Expected values must not be generated by production noise or rate helpers.
- [ ] Exercise actual generator advancement for all 32 FLG rates across two shared-counter wraps. Check held values between events, rate-zero holding and rate-31 advancement. Include explicit rate-2 events at ticks `1040/2576`, rate-3 events at `536/1816`, and rate-29 events at `2/5/8` under the retained sample convention. Verify live rate changes preserve phase.
- [ ] Cover every NON bit, simultaneous selected voices sharing one sequence, mixed BRR/noise voices, NON toggles without reseeding, pitch independence, and continued BRR/ENDX progression using original looping and non-looping data. Check envelope scaling, OUTX, signed left/right volumes and EON routing with numerical assertions that avoid relying on unverified echo saturation.
- [ ] Verify generator continuity through no active voices, NON=0, mute, key-on delay, KOFF and FLG voice reset. Verify fresh DSP/machine reset reproduces the defined initialization. Preserve existing five-sample key-on and release behavior.
- [ ] Add an original in-memory SPC700 guest in `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_noise.rs`, uploaded through the existing IPL protocol. It must configure NON/FLG through `$F2/$F3`, record numerical OUTX checkpoints in RAM, and exercise a live rate or NON change. Use explicit execution/acknowledgement limits and checkpoints away from subcycle boundaries. Document original source/data and MIT provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; require no firmware, downloaded binary or commercial ROM.
- [ ] Add APU integration coverage comparing every PCM sample and relevant DSP registers between whole and irregularly partitioned master-clock advancement, including noise-rate changes, mute/unmute and shared-counter wraps. Require finite bounded output and independent numerical checkpoints, not just matching runs or non-silence.
- [ ] Preserve existing DSP/envelope/ENDX regressions, original diagnostic bytes, fixture pins/hashes and all cleared-game assertions and replay durations. Pass the existing workspace, source-built hardware and browser checks documented in [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/63a136517e53e074dede3f47a74fd2040d583ae3/README.md#validate):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test -p snes-core --test dsp_noise --locked
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
cd web
npx playwright install chromium
SNES_TEST_PORT=18085 npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Use the README's compiler-selection override where needed. The browser run must retain both cleared five-minute game replays, Castle's complete route and negative control, Memory's numerical/live audio checks, and diagnostic/Pages checks. Excluding optional unaudited games must not exclude cleared-game regressions.

- [ ] Update README and a focused validation record with baseline failure evidence, exact commands/results, source attribution and coverage limits. Explicitly retain remaining noise-related gaps: subcycle NON/FLG sampling, register-write races and interactions with still-unimplemented pitch modulation. All other 24 inventory categories retain their supplied scope, status and outstanding work. Limited passing tests establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility and do not complete historical partial Issue #3 work.

## Optional validation

None. Commercial ROM acquisition, subjective listening and physical-device approval are not required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
